synthesis.overnight_summary: Hot US September CPI (3.7% headline, 2.6% core) sent gold down ~2% to a five-day low near $4,073 as October hike odds doubled to ~44% and the dollar hit an 18-month high; MCX Dec gold fell ~Rs 2,600 to 145,850 and silver dropped ~6.7%. Overnight the move largely reversed: a Bloomberg report that China is holding Treasuries via Canada pulled the US 10Y back to ~5.10%, the dollar fell 0.5% and oil eased, lifting spot ~1% to ~$4,144. Fed speakers stayed hawkish (Daly sees more hikes but no urgency in October; Goolsbee called CPI 'discouraging'), and October hike odds settled near ~32%. The model puts the MCX fair open at ~Rs 148,405 (+Rs 2,555), almost back to the 13-Oct close, with the rupee a small plus. Expect a sharp gap-up open that then has to prove itself against still-hawkish Fed pricing, today's US PPI/retail sales at 18:00 IST and Warsh tomorrow morning.
